source.title: Universal Scaling Laws in Quantum-Probabilistic Machine Learning by Tensor Network: Toward Interpreting Representation and Generalization Powers

record.tranche_reason: Measures negative-log-likelihood scaling in generative tensor networks on image and other datasets, an extension to a different model and training setting. Its scaling variables and reported functional forms differ from the language-model parameter, token, and compute laws in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports NLL scaling against feature count M, virtual dimension χ, and training-sample count N. These results are recorded for V5. It also reports classification accuracy and feature-map orthogonality results, but they do not measure the scaling form named in the claim versions and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study trains MPS generative tensor networks on image and sensor data and reports how NLL scales with parameter complexity (χ) and training-sample count (N). That is a non-language setting bearing on V5. The headline laws are in feature count M (input size), which is not a parameter, data or compute axis. The χ and N results are logarithmic fits, not power laws.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely right. It should add that the authors report NLL and its coefficients scaling logarithmically with χ and with training-sample count N. They read the χ>30 train/test divergence as over-parameterization, and the train/test gap in N as a test of data sufficiency.
record.recipe_differences: Uses generative tensor networks in matrix-product-state form and studies NLL as a function of feature count and virtual dimension, rather than language-model parameter, token, or compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported coefficients vary with χ, dataset, binarization, and training versus testing set; for about χ > 30 the testing coefficients deviate from the training trend.

fits_no_version.finding: In MPS generative tensor networks, NLL grows linearly with the number of input features M for an untrained or mismatched model (k ≈ 0.18 gray-scale, ≈ 1.3–1.6 binarized). After training it follows βM − αM² + γ, across Fashion-MNIST, MNIST, KMNIST and HAR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-sample NLL of tensor-network generative models scales linearly in input dimensionality (orthogonality catastrophe), with a negative quadratic correction once trained.

record.problems: The experiments concern GTNs and datasets rather than language models, and vary feature count and virtual dimension rather than parameter count, training tokens, or compute. Several dataset results are shown in figures without numeric fits in the text; the text does not provide fit uncertainties for the reported coefficients.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted classification accuracy, average probability, and quantum-feature-map orthogonality results because they do not measure the scaling forms in the tested claim version. No scaling results were omitted for space.

untested.parts: Power-law scaling in compute; video or other neural generative models; repeated data; fine-tuning; transfer. The study never compares a power-law fit against its log fits.
All of it. Classification accuracy is reported, but not as scale-predictability.

missing.what: Intra-class NLL versus virtual dimension χ for training and testing sets, fitted as L ≃ pL ln χ + qL. This is the paper's direct loss-versus-parameter-complexity result; no numeric pL or qL appears in the text.
Logarithmic scaling of the α and β coefficients against χ (α ≃ pα ln χ + qα), fitted on training data.

record.verdict_notes: The model is a quantum-inspired tensor network, not a neural network, so its link to the neural scaling-law claim is loose. The 'universal scaling laws' are mainly in feature count M, which is not a scaling-law axis in the claim's sense. The χ range is small (about 2–128), so a log fit and a small-exponent power law may be hard to tell apart. The authors don't compare the two.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss of language models versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between parameters and tokens.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The paper studies GTNs, including image and other datasets, but does not test video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or language-model parameter/token/compute scaling.
Predictability of downstream language-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Whether language-model exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on fitting or setup choices, or whether those language-model curves bend.

rows.subject: GTN in the MPS form
rows.operation_detail: Compares training and testing coefficient and NLL scaling against virtual dimension χ
rows.measure: Difference in scaling behavior between training and testing sets
rows.value: For about χ > 30, training coefficients maintain the stated logarithmic behavior; testing coefficients start to deviate, with higher testing NLL.
rows.note: Authors interpret this as representation improvement continuing while generalization improvement decelerates, a sign of over-parameterization.
rows.check: Held-out NLL still improves with χ (a parameter axis). Above about χ>30 the test coefficients depart from the training log trend and test NLL is higher. The trend is logarithmic in χ, not a power law.

rows.subject: GTN in the MPS form
rows.operation_detail: Fits NLL against number of training samples N
rows.measure: Convergence of scaling coefficients with N
rows.value: Coefficients for training and testing converge to the same values as N increases; no numeric values stated.
rows.note: The authors say the discrepancy can be used to judge whether training data are sufficient.
rows.check: Reports only the logarithmic behaviour of the α, β, γ coefficients against N, and train/test convergence. No NLL value or fitted form is given in the text.

relationships.condition: MPS generative tensor networks on Fashion-MNIST (M=784), scaling in virtual dimension χ and training samples N
relationships.reason: NLL falls with χ but is fitted as L ≃ pL ln χ + qL, a logarithmic rather than power-law form (Fig. 3d, text-based; see missing). Coefficients are also logarithmic in N (R35). Test NLL departs from the trend above χ≈30 (R34).
relationships.display_finding: NLL decreased logarithmically with χ, fitted coefficients depended logarithmically on N, and test NLL departed from the trend above χ ≈ 30.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GTN/MPS NLL scaling on Fashion-MNIST and the other listed datasets
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports scaling against feature count M and virtual dimension χ, with linear or linear-plus-quadratic forms, rather than testing the claimed language-model parameter/token/compute power laws; the results therefore establish only a narrower, setting-specific extension (R1–R35).
